review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

3:1.sourceText: Διὸ μηκέτι στέγοντες ηὐδοκήσαμεν καταλειφθῆναι ἐν Ἀθήναις μόνοι,
3:1.targetText: For this reason, enduring no longer, we thought good to be left in Athens alone,

3:2.sourceText: καὶ ἐπέμψαμεν Τιμόθεον, τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἡμῶν καὶ διάκονον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, εἰς τὸ στηρίξαι ὑμᾶς καὶ παρακαλέσαι ὑπὲρ τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν
3:2.targetText: and sent Timotheus—our brother, and a servant of God, and our fellow-workman in the good news of the Christ—to establish you, and to comfort you concerning your faith,

groups.note: The articular purpose infinitive εἰς τὸ στηρίξαι is expressed by English to establish as a single grammatical constituent; no independent English preposition is invented.
The one N1904 ὑμᾶς supplies the shared object of establish and comfort, repeated as you in both English limbs. TR also repeats ὑμᾶς after comfort.

N1904 ὑπέρ, here on behalf of/concerning your faith, corresponds contextually to concerning; TR instead has περί. The same discourse relation is retained without claiming the preposition readings are identical.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness difference: LSV follows TR καὶ συνεργὸν ἡμῶν; N1904 has no corresponding fellow-worker noun, pronoun or conjunction.

3:3.sourceText: τὸ μηδένα σαίνεσθαι ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσιν ταύταις. αὐτοὶ γὰρ οἴδατε ὅτι εἰς τοῦτο κείμεθα·
3:3.targetText: that no one be moved in these tribulations, for you have known that we are set for this,

groups.note: The article introducing the infinitival clause τὸ μηδένα σαίνεσθαι marks the intended/result clause, rendered that no one be moved; that is its syntactic role here, not a lexical equation for articles generally.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

3:4.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ ὅτε πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἦμεν, προελέγομεν ὑμῖν ὅτι μέλλομεν θλίβεσθαι, καθὼς καὶ ἐγένετο καὶ οἴδατε.
3:4.targetText: for even when we were with you, we said to you beforehand that we are about to suffer tribulation, as it also came to pass, and you have known [it];

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English object supplied for have known; no separate accusative pronoun occurs with οἴδατε.

3:5.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο κἀγὼ μηκέτι στέγων ἔπεμψα εἰς τὸ γνῶναι τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν, μή πως ἐπείρασεν ὑμᾶς ὁ πειράζων καὶ εἰς κενὸν γένηται ὁ κόπος ἡμῶν.
3:5.targetText: because of this also, I, no longer enduring, sent to know your faith, lest he who is tempting tempted you, and our labor might be in vain.

groups.note: The articular purpose infinitive εἰς τὸ γνῶναι is expressed as English to know; these syntactically joined source words share that constituent.

3:6.sourceText: Ἄρτι δὲ ἐλθόντος Τιμοθέου πρὸς ἡμᾶς ἀφ’ ὑμῶν καὶ εὐαγγελισαμένου ἡμῖν τὴν πίστιν καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην ὑμῶν, καὶ ὅτι ἔχετε μνείαν ἡμῶν ἀγαθὴν πάντοτε, ἐπιποθοῦντες ἡμᾶς ἰδεῖν καθάπερ καὶ ἡμεῖς ὑμᾶς,
3:6.targetText: And Timotheus now having come to us from you, and having declared good news to us of your faith and love, and that you always have a good remembrance of us, desiring much to see us, as we also [to see] you,

groups.note: The Greek object faith of the good-news reporting verb is rendered with English of faith; of is the English noun/verb complement construction, not an extra Greek preposition.

3:8.sourceText: ὅτι νῦν ζῶμεν ἐὰν ὑμεῖς στήκετε ἐν Κυρίῳ.
3:8.targetText: because now we live, if you may stand fast in the LORD.

groups.note: The conditional standing-fast predicate is rendered may stand fast. N1904 spells στήκετε with indicative-form epsilon whereas TR στήκητε is subjunctive; the same lexical predicate and recipients are retained with the mood-form difference recorded.

3:10.sourceText: νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ δεόμενοι εἰς τὸ ἰδεῖν ὑμῶν τὸ πρόσωπον καὶ καταρτίσαι τὰ ὑστερήματα τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν;
3:10.targetText: exceedingly imploring night and day, that we might see your face, and perfect the things lacking in your faith?

groups.note: The genitive τῆς πίστεως qualifies things lacking; LSV expresses this genitive relation as in your faith. The noun phrase is kept together rather than falsely assigning in to an isolated article.

3:11.sourceText: Αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Πατὴρ ἡμῶν καὶ ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς κατευθύναι τὴν ὁδὸν ἡμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς·
3:11.targetText: And our God and Father Himself, and our Lord Jesus Christ, direct our way to you,

groups.note: Greek κατευθύναι is an optative wish that God and the Lord direct their way. LSV uses bare direct for the same wish, not a claim that the Greek is an imperative.

3:12.sourceText: ὑμᾶς δὲ ὁ Κύριος πλεονάσαι καὶ περισσεύσαι τῇ ἀγάπῃ εἰς ἀλλήλους καὶ εἰς πάντας, καθάπερ καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς ὑμᾶς,
3:12.targetText: and the LORD cause you to increase and to abound in the love to one another, and to all, even as we also to you,

groups.note: The transitive optative πλεονάσαι is rendered cause ... to increase, sharing its object you with the coordinated cause-to-abound predicate.
The dative phrase τῇ ἀγάπῃ is rendered by English in the love; in expresses the sphere/instrumental case relation of the whole phrase, not a separate Greek preposition.

3:13.sourceText: εἰς τὸ στηρίξαι ὑμῶν τὰς καρδίας ἀμέμπτους ἐν ἁγιωσύνῃ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ μετὰ πάντων τῶν ἁγίων αὐτοῦ.
3:13.targetText: in order to have established your hearts, blameless in sanctification before our God and Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all His holy ones.

groups.note: The aorist infinitive στηρίξαι establishes the intended outcome, rendered English have established. The perfect English phrasing does not add another Greek finite have verb.
